title: offset d construction — shrink constant k x shrink target (self / league), 7 x 2 grid, selected on prior-season blocks
stage: stage 1 only, seed 42.  No model is trained; three stage-1 prediction vectors are reused byte-for-byte (sha asserted).
changed_vs_exp_022: the EB shrink constant k of the personal (pitcher, batter_hand) estimate is swept over [0,30,55,111,200,400,800]; exp_022 held it at the exp_018 value 111 throughout
the same k also sets the league term's weight k/(n+k) in the `league` target (exp_022 G2 used 111 there)
the arm is CHOSEN on supply blocks 2022+2023; exp_022 reported all arms on fold_2024 with no selection step
beta is re-fitted per arm on the same blocks (unchanged in kind, but its value moves with k — it is a dependent output, not an axis)
unchanged_vs_exp_022: base prediction vectors (fold_2024 and both blocks), iter 650/170, seed 42, exp_004 F-mask, clip bounds 1e-6, closed-form no-intercept slope estimator, supply blocks 2022+2023, league table code (backoff.py byte-identical, sha asserted)

reproduction_gate.arm: k=111 x self at the CONTROL beta = exp_022 G1f (BK1f) = the d of deployed candidates H/I
reproduction_gate.on_fail: abort — the inherited code or the reused predictions are not exp_022's and nothing downstream is readable

same_arm_with_REFITTED_beta.note: this is exp_022 G1 (0.2480365266).  It also sits inside 5e-6 of G1f, which is why the gate is run at the control beta — otherwise it would pass for the wrong reason.

k111_equivalence.why: the literal form's miss row is (k*o)/k - o, which IEEE-754 does not guarantee to be 0.  It held at k=111 by luck and broke at k=200 (first launch died on season 2021).  Same bug class exp_022 fixed in the league term by regrouping to L*(k/(n+k)).

anchor_check.k0_degeneracy_note: at k=0 there is no shrinkage, so the league term gets weight 0 on hit rows and weight 1 (the limit from k->0+) on miss rows — which is the hard backoff.  The two targets coincide.  13 distinct arms, not 14.

asof_independent_recheck.method: row_id -> season re-read from train.csv in a second pass; the table masks are re-derived and the max season of the CONTRIBUTING ROW IDS is looked up in that independent map

selection.rule: argmin Brier on supply blocks 2022+2023, beta fitted on the same blocks.  fold_2024 is read only after this line.

selection_cost.note: the fold_2024 argmin is what cheating would have bought.  It is reported to price the discipline, not to be adopted.

n_bin_definition.note: n_cell is the (pitcher, batter_hand) cell count that fed the row's shrunk estimate.  miss_n0 rows have no personal cell at all; `fx_*` are fixed cuts, the others are hit-row tertiles.

league_target_risk.warning: the `league` target pushes L onto CELL-HIT rows too, so the pitcher-hand-2 cells — whose L flips sign across vintages (exp_022 audit) — reach rows that the hard backoff never touched.  A local gain does not retire this risk.

conversion.sensitivity: brier 1e-6 = score 0.4003; a 6-decimal Brier carries +-0.2002 in the converted number
conversion.caveat: local measurement is at iter 650 (<=2023 training); the deployed build is iter 7700 (<=2024).  Every number here carries that caveat.

leak_boundary.tables: row of season s uses seasons <= s-1 only; verified twice — at runtime, and independently by re-reading train.csv and looking the contributing row_ids' seasons up again
leak_boundary.design_matrix: unchanged — no deviation is ever a model feature
leak_boundary.missing: no sentinel fill anywhere; L=0 and d=0 are the estimators' own no-op outputs
